Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements (DTAAs): Mexico, South Korea, Spain, Singapore, Luxembourg, Qatar, France, Barbados, Portugal, United Arab Emirates, Netherlands (verify active status); OECD Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) Inclusive Framework membership

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley No. 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (decreto reglamentario: Decreto Ejecutivo No. 363 de 4 de agosto de 2015);  Decreto Ejecutivo No. 201 de 26 de octubre de 2017 (Reglamento de la Unidad de Análisis Financiero - UAF);  Ley 70 de 2019 (transparencia y beneficiario final);  Decreto de Gabinete No. 8 de 7 de febrero de 2020 (Sistema de Información de Beneficiario Final - registro de beneficiario final ante la DGI, administrado actualmente por la Dirección General de Ingresos y la Unidad de Análisis Financiero);  Código de Comercio de Panamá (Arts. 99-106 y correlativos);  Ley No. 52 de 2016 (factoring y sociedades; no aplicable directamente);  Reglamento de Debida Diligencia de la UAF (Acuerdo 3-2024 y resoluciones complementarias).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (Beneficiario final declarado ante el Registro Único de Beneficiario Final de la DGI; acceso restringido a autoridades tributarias, UAF, Ministerio Público y entes de supervisión; no es registro público abierto. Sin embargo, el Registro Público conserva la identidad del accionista titular si no se usa nominatario; con uso de accionistas nominativos o fundaciones de interés privado el acceso real se limita a la declaración gubernamental).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency and Corporate Good Standing (Certificado de Personería Jurídica, emitted by Registro Público de Panamá) for any foreign parent entity, if shareholder is a juridical person
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registro Público de Panamá (historical; new filings via Registro de Personas Jurídicas) or equivalent foreign company registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention (Panama acceded; apostille by competent authority of the issuing jurisdiction; if a non-Hague jurisdiction, full consular legalization chain required)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Copy of Articles of Incorporation (Pacto Social y Estatutos) of the foreign shareholder, duly translated into Spanish and authenticated
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign Corporate Registry or Notary Public of the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization at the Panamanian Consulate in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (Poder Especial) for the incorporating attorney or agent, executed before a Panamanian Notary or authenticated abroad
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notario Público de Panamá or foreign notary with apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Fiel Cumplimiento) of the proposed director and resident agent, if required by the Registro Público
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registro Público de Panamá / relevant professional association (Colegio de Abogados)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: AML/KYC Bank-Reference Package for UBO: certified passport copy, proof of residential address, banker's reference or source-of-funds declaration for each ultimate beneficial owner (mandatory under Law 23/2015 for the resident agent law firm when acting as gatekeeper)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public, certified translation agency, and licensed financial institution of the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization combined with notarization and sworn translation into Spanish

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate Accounting and Statutory Books Opening Protocol (Libro de Accionistas, Libro de Actas de Directorio y Junta, Registro de Beneficiario Final interno) with notarized due diligence minutes
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notario Público de Panamá and the incorporated S.A.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all identified UBOs, directors, officers, resident agents, and beneficial owners against: (1) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List; (2) United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (3) European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (4) UK HMT Consolidated List; (5) Panamanian National Counter-Terrorism List (Ley 30 de 2013); (6) Financial Action Task Force (FATF) High-Risk Jurisdictions list; (7) World Bank and IADB debarment lists for payroll integration contracts. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) mandatory for all politically exposed persons (PEPs), including immediate family members and close associates, with source-of-wealth documentation, senior management approval, and a 24-month ongoing transaction monitoring plan. Negative news screening and adverse media check (SanctionsAdvisor, Dow Jones, LexisNexis equivalent) required within 72 hours prior to incorporation and every 12 months thereafter.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_filing_obligation: The Resident Agent (agente residente) must file the Declaración de Beneficiario Final with the DGI within 30 days of incorporation and within 15 days of any UBO change; failure results in fines up to USD 500,000 for the company and suspension of corporate rights (Ley 70 de 2019).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá - Sistema de Navegación y Consulta de Personas Jurídicas (at www.registropublico.gob.pa; online name reservation via 'Consulta de Nombre de Sociedad' and 'Apartado de Nombre'; the exact current portal module is 'Sistema de Personas Jurídicas' operated by the Dirección General de Registro de Personas Jurídicas).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate names must be inscribed on the SEPARATION BUTTON (Separación de Nombre) in Spanish or in a transliterated Latin-script version. The Registro Público requires that the corporate name include a preposition, noun, trademark, or expression that distinguishes it from all existing registrations. If the base name is in English, a Spanish transliteration is mandatory for the registered suffix; however, the fully English trademark portion may be preserved with a Spanish descriptive addition. Names must end with the abbreviation 'S.A.' or the full 'Sociedad Anónima'. Cómo: the Registro Público accepts names in 'any language' as long as they use the Latin alphabet, but the practice requires a Spanish-language term or distinctive word to facilitate registry. The transliteration must match the phonetic rendition in the apostilled documents; a forensic name-conflict search in Spanish, English, and any other language used by the corporate group is mandatory.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In case of name rejection, the incorporator or attorney may: (1) Request a reconsideration (recurso de reconsideración) before the Dirección General de Personas Jurídicas within 5 business days of the rejection notice, providing a memorandum distinguishing the proposed name from the conflicting registration; (2) If reconsideration fails, file a jurisdictional appeal (recurso de apelación) before the Registro General (Dirección General del Registro Público), also within 5 business days; (3) Submit a request for a new name option of the same corporate object without incurring new statutory fees. In high-conflict cases, a pre-registration non-use waiver from the similarly-named company may be obtained; alternatively, seek an administrative injunction (amparo de garantías) before the Panamanian Contentious Administrative Court if fundamental procedural rights are violated. Practical recommendation: reserve 2-3 fallback names at the time of the initial filing to avoid re-filing delays; each reservation costs an administrative fee and the reservation window of 30 days is not extendable; after 30 days a new reservation with a new filing fee is required. The name reservation is non-renewable for identical wording, but modified variants (adding a geographic or activity descriptor) may be filed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Yes, with conditions. The S.A. must maintain a physical registered office (oficina registrada) in Panama, which is necessarily the address of the resident agent (agente residente) — a licensed lawyer or law firm. Virtual office and business-center addressing are permissible only as the registered agent's service address; a separate administrative office may be virtual for operational purposes. However, for a payroll SaaS platform processing Latin American payroll for clients and targeting financial institution integration via Direct Debit ACH and Swift Wire, the Panamanian banking regulator (Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá) and financial counterparties will require a functional operational address, not merely a virtual box, to establish business banking relationships. The registered agent address must be a physical street address in line with the Registro Público standards; commercial virtual offices (e.g., Regus, WeWork) are acceptable as the
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate for the administrative address if the company holds a PayPal/Stripe or local acquirer contract or applies for a banking license. Background under current Panamanian practice: the Registro Público does not conduct routine physical inspections; however, the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), the Municipality of Panama (Domiciliación Fiscal), and the Social Security Fund (CSS) may conduct unannounced tax inspections after registration of a payroll SaaS with any payment processing (even via third-party rails). Probability quantification: 30% in the first fiscal year if only standard payroll software activities are conducted; up to 60% if the UBO is flagged in the PEP or sanctions screening or if transactions occur in high-risk jurisdictions. Annual tax domicile verification (comprobación de domicilio fiscal) is required from year two.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 32 de 1927 (General Corporation Law), as amended; applicable Arts. 1–13 (incorporation), Art. 36 (registered office), Art. 46 (directors and officers)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Mercantile Section
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (notarized deed of incorporation) submitted as a certified copy for inscription
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement; the Company may declare authorized capital and issue shares without mandatory deposit, escrow, or capitalization evidence.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS MEETING, [DATE]. RESOLVED: (1) To accept the subscription of the initial shares and to certify issued share capital. (2) To adopt the registered office indicated in the Articles and to maintain statutory addresses with the Public Registry. (3) To appoint the CEO, CFO, and Corporate Secretary, granting joint authority to act in banking and corporate transactions. (4) To open bank accounts and complete all tax, municipal, and social-security registrations. (5) To authorize the Secretary to execute all instruments and filings necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sistema Integrado de Servicios en Línea (SISI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a preliminary name availability search on the SISI online portal. If available, submit a Solicitud de Reserva de Nombre; the reservation is valid for 30 calendar days and can be renewed for an additional term. The name must conform to the mandatory suffix 'Sociedad Anónima' or the abbreviation 'S.A.'
required_dossiers: Copy of applicant's passport or Panamanian cedula
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or allegedly confusing, the registry will list similar entries. The applicant may file an alternative name immediately; objections may be overcome by presenting a letter of consent or abandonment of the conflicting name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Escritura Pública de Constitución
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario Público del Circuito de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the articles of incorporation containing corporate name, domicile, corporate purpose, authorized capital, term, and initial directors. Have each incorporator or authorized representative sign the deeds before a Panamanian notary. The notary will issue the authenticated public deed and certified copy for presentation to the Public Registry.
required_dossiers: Passport or ID of each incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a notarial defect or missing clause is detected, the incorporators execute an amendment (reforma) before the same or another notary and the corrected deed is re-submitted. Registry notificaciones explain the specific omission and are cured by the re-executed document.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Company with the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Mercantile Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pay the official registration fee and national stamp duty on the registry's online system or via the DGPN treasury. Submit the certified notarial copy, fee payment receipt, and an explanatory cover sheet to the Mercantile Section for inscription. After review, the Public Registry grants the company's Ficha (corporate identification) and the Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the Escritura Pública de Constitución
Proof of payment of official fees and stamp duty
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry returns a diligencias or correction notice, the company may cure the issue by amending the deed and resubmitting within the statutory period. Minor deviations may be remedied through a clarification writ directed to the mercantile registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organization of Corporate Governance and Statutory Books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Book-Sealing Office and Company Internal Governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the First Board of Directors meeting, adopt the pro-forma board resolution, and record the resolutions in the corporate minute book. Issue share certificates and open the Share Ledger. Register the statutory corporate books with the Public Registry for sealing, including the minutes, share transfer, and shareholders register.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the First Board of Directors meeting
Corporate records (share ledger, board minutes book, officers registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the book-sealing office rejects books for pagination or certification defects, correct the book bindings and certify the pages before a notary, then re-submit for sealing. Once sealed, no corrections may be inserted except by formal issuance of replacement folios.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Municipal Operating License (Aviso de Operación)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Municipio de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the Public Registry issues the Certificate of Incorporation, register for the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) through the DGI online portal. Subsequently, file the annual municipal operating license application via the Municipality of Panama's Aviso de Operación system, attaching the corporate certificate and proof of commercial premises.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or property title of the registered office
Municipal Aviso de Operación application form
Tax payer identification form (607/608 if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Municipality requires physical address verification, provide a certified lease and laminated address notice. In case of tax registration errors, the DGI allows online corrections; any rejected application can be revised and submitted within the voluntary correction window.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI); Municipio de Panamá – Directorate of License and Operations
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación de Empresa (Annual Municipal Operating License)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Environmental Impact Assessment Directorate
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 1 – Environmental Registration; no full EIA required for office-based payroll software services.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or combustion emission thresholds apply. The operation must comply with general solid waste management rules under MiAMBIENTE Resolution AG-0244-2019 and proper handling of hazardous electronic waste, if any.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and certification from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá; structural and electrical load clearance from the Municipality of Panama; workplace hygiene and occupational health clearance from the Ministerio de Trabajo (MITRADEL) and CSS.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) - General Directorate of Revenues, Ministry of Economy and Finance (Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, MEF). Online portal: SIT - Sistema de Información Tributaria (https://sit.dgi.gob.pa), with e-filing, registry and electronic-invoice validation services; ancillary site: https://www.dgi.gob.pa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign-owned Panama S.A. must obtain its RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) through the DGI within 30 days after inscription of the incorporation deed in the Registro Público of Panama. Procedure: (i) file the Aviso de Operación (Notice of Operations) with DGI Form 1410; (ii) upload the public deed, the Registro Público certificate, board resolution appointing a resident legal representative, and the IMF (Información de Accionistas/beneficiario final under Law 23/2015); (iii) obtain the 11-digit RUC for 'Persona Jurídica con fines de lucro'; (iv) activate the taxpayer profile as general-regime (no simplified small-taxpayer cap at B/. 123,000 annual revenue); (v) request habilitación under DGI Resolution 201-1521/2022 for mandatory electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica en Línea - FEL) and register the fiscal accounting books (SIC - Sistema de Información Contable); (vi) if SaaS exports to non-residents are intended, file the DGI 'Registro de Exportador de Servicios' application under Decreto Ejecutivo 84 de 2005 to support 0% ITBMS treatment and territorial-source deferral until repatriation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation / Territorial_Scope : The Panama S.A. (Sociedad Anónima) is a resident legal entity subject to entity-level income tax under the territorial system; only Panama-source income is taxed, including services exported from Panama once the consideration is deemed received/repatriated (overall no CFC or worldwide taxation rules). The S.A. cannot be classified as a pass-through; dividends paid to non-resident shareholders are subject to a 5%/10% dividend tax (with a 4%/7.5% advance credit system depending on the source income taxed under the normal rate).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists. Available statutory elections: (i) alternatively, the taxpayer may elect to compute income tax under the 'normal profit-based' method versus the presumptive minimum gross-income method (Art. 699-I Código Fiscal), with the larger amount payable; (ii) election to use the simplified fixed-rate cash method for small taxpayers is unavailable to PA_CORP given the B/. 123,000 revenue cap; (iii) election to be treated as an 'empresa exportadora de servicios' under Decree 84/2005 - automatically renewing for each fiscal year - which preserves 0% ITBMS and taxation of export income upon repatriation (explicit board resolution and DGI registry); (iv) hybrid mismatch elections: not available; Panama has not adopted OECD hybrid-mismatch or check-the-box rules, and treaty benefits under Panama's limited income-tax treaty network require actual residency and beneficial-ownership substantiation rather than an entity classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) - a value-added/consumption tax equivalent to VAT
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/. 123,000 (Panama Balboa, pegged 1:1 to USD) annual gross revenue cap for the Simplified Small-Taxpayer Regime; there is no de minimis threshold for general-regime ITBMS registration, and any taxable transfer of goods or rendering of services within Panama triggers the obligation to register, charge and remit ITBMS from the first taxable event, with monthly returns filed via the SIT portal.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory FEL (Facturación Electrónica en Línea) for all general-regime taxpayers under DGI Resolution 201-1521/2022, fully effective for the 2024 tax year. Invoices must be transmitted to the DGI SIT platform in near-real-time through DGI-certified electronic invoicing service providers or a direct DGI API integration; the DGI applies a 'conciliación/validación' clearance step, validates the RUC, business name, revenue type and fiscal folio sequence, and returns a unique electronic security code (código único de facturación / QR) that must be embedded on the PDF/XML copy delivered to the client. Credit notes, debit notes and export zero-rated invoices follow the same pre-authorization/clearance flow; fiscal printers may remain in use only for the simplified small-taxpayer regime, not for PA_CORP.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and 'exportación de servicios' are taxed at 0% ITBMS under Art. 1054 Código Fiscal and Art. 53 of Law 25/1995. For ISIC 6201 (Automated Global Payroll and Staff Compliance Software as a Service), the S.A. must prove: (i) the SaaS subscription contract is executed with a non-resident recipient; (ii) the service is technically rendered from Panama but effectively used/benefited abroad; (iii) consideration is invoiced in a freely convertible foreign currency accepted by the DGI (USD/Balboa is acceptable); (iv) payment is remitted to a Panamanian bank account from abroad; and (v) the S.A. is registered as an export service company with the DGI. Upon compliance, input ITBMS on payroll software development, cloud costs and local overhead becomes creditable against 0% output, generating an ITBMS credit/refund position and an income-tax deferral of territorial-source service revenue until funds actually enter Panama.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única de Exportación / DAU transmitted via SISICEA) for any physical goods or embedded hardware component
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing the goods exported; for pure SaaS, the executed subscription contract and hosting/delivery records (server logs) replace the transport document

Certificado de Ingreso de Divisas (Inward Remittance Certificate) or certified bank statement of the Panamanian licensed bank showing the incoming ACH/SWIFT wire from the foreign client, matched to the export invoice
Duly executed international SaaS license/subscription agreement and the monthly usage/statement of work, evidencing the non-resident recipient and economic benefit abroad
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI may audit export zero-rating files for 5 fiscal years, extended to 7 years if omission or fraud is detected. Failure to maintain the mandatory documentation bundle, or claiming zero-rating without actual receipt of foreign funds within the 180-day administrative window, triggers retrospective clawback of all ITBMS credits/refunds claimed, plus moratory interest (statutory rate of 10% per annum) and a 50% surcharge on the recaptured tax; false or materially misleading export declarations constitute tax fraud under Panama's penal-tax provisions (Law 70/2019), carrying fines from B/. 1,000 to B/. 10,000 per infraction, administrative sanctions equal to 100% of the evaded tax, and possible imprisonment of 2 to 5 years for aggravated cases. The DGI also applies per-article fines under Art. 746 Código Fiscal for non-archival of export documents and may notify the financial-intelligence unit for AML-linked invoice fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama has no conventional central bank. The Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) is the primary banking regulator and Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as the government's fiscal agent and clearing channel for public-sector transactions. Monetary policy is effectively determined by the U.S. Federal Reserve because Panama is fully dollarized with the U.S. dollar as legal tender.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates a fully dollarized, freely convertible monetary system. There are no exchange-control laws, no prior import or export license requirements for foreign exchange transactions, and no restrictions on the movement of capital for current-account or capital-account purposes. Profit remittance through dividends, capital reductions, or intercompany loan repayments is lawful and does not require central bank approval; the only statutory condition is the prior settlement of any applicable Panamanian taxes, including dividend taxes or branch remittance taxes, and compliance with the company's corporate records and beneficial ownership disclosure obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama does not impose mandatory export proceeds surrender, repatriation deadlines, or minimum conversion ratios. Exporters may retain proceeds in foreign currency or U.S. dollars in any Panamanian or foreign bank account. The only obligation is to record the transactions accurately for tax and anti-money-laundering purposes in compliance with SBP regulations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-Low feasibility as the primary settlement rail. Offshore fintech electronic money institutions are not licensed or supervised by the SBP and therefore cannot provide the same legal certainty, statutory protection, or local clearing access as a Panamanian licensed bank. Such EMIs may be used as ancillary receiving channels for inbound client payments or for disbursements to sub-contractors in certain jurisdictions, but the core payroll escrow and treasury function should sit with a locally licensed commercial bank to permit ACH clearing, direct debit, SWIFT MT103 outbound wires, and SBP-regulated dispute resolution. Any foreign EMI must demonstrate a correspondent banking relationship with a Panamanian bank and comply with SBP KYC expectations for virtual account providers.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Panama does not impose a universal statutory requirement that all directors attend a bank branch in person. In practice, for a non-resident owned Sociedad Anónima with the benefit of an appointed resident agent, most Tier-1 banks accept a remote video interview for the legal representative, beneficial owner, and signatories, provided the documents are certified by a Panama-licensed attorney and, where requested, corroborated through a bank officer or compliance officer visit. Some banks require the authorized signatory to appear physically at a branch or at the resident agent's office for the final documentary authentication. Enhanced due diligence for a payroll SaaS platform will generally require at least one senior compliance interview, whether in person or by video, with the ultimate beneficial owner and the compliance officer of the operating entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The S.A. has opaque ownership structures, nominee shareholders, or legacy bearer-share instruments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Registro Público corporate chisel record; certified shareholder ledger; nominee disclosure declarations; notarized UBO declarations for all natural persons holding 10% or more; basic identity documents, tax identification numbers, and evidence of the legal chain from the transfer agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The payroll software serves high-risk clients in sanctioned, embargoed, or unreliable-reporting jurisdictions, or an unusually high volume of mass low-value disbursements to third parties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete client jurisdiction list; automated sanctions-screening results; internal anti-money-laundering and sanctions-compliance manual; customer risk classification matrix; sample CDD files for major payroll clients; written rationale for the payment-rail design and evidence of transaction monitoring controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital contributions originate from non-bank payment intermediaries, cryptocurrency exchanges, or lower-tier foreign banks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-funds declaration explaining the capital injection; original bank statements from the sending institution; audited financial statements or management accounts of the investing entity; notarized board resolution approving the capital increase; confirmation that the beneficial owner of the contributing funds is the same as the S.A. beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The S.A. has been newly incorporated and has no local economic substance, no local employees, and no prior tax filing history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Resident-agent letter confirming legal existence and operation address; draft employment statements for any local contractor; business plan for the Panama office or registered agent services; tax registration (RUC) if applicable; evidence of external accounting and registered office fees; AML/KYC questionnaire describing management and oversight of the payroll processing activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The directors or signatories are politically exposed persons (PEPs) or fail to provide independent wealth evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP self-declaration forms; source-of-wealth reports; professional reference letters from a regulated financial institution; negative media-search reports; corroborating employment or business-ownership documentation; notarised identity documents and proof of residential address.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections must be made by SWIFT international wire or correspondent-bank transfer from the investing company's or beneficial owner's regulated bank account into the S.A.'s stated USD account in Panama. The wire instruction must identify the S.A. as beneficiary by exact legal name and bank account number, include the bank SWIFT/BIC, and in the payment narrative clearly state 'Capital Contribution to Sociedad Anónima' or 'Share Capital Subscription'. No Central Bank approval or exchange-control permit is required. For enhanced compliance, the company should provide the receiving bank with a certified shareholders' meeting resolution approving the capital increase, an updated share registry, and an undertaking to file the relevant corporate amendment with the Registro Público if the contribution is formalized through a share issue. The remitter should avoid combining payroll operating funds with one-off capital subscriptions in the same wire; separate references should be used to allow clean audit trail segregation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Payroll settlements and trade disbursements should use SWIFT MT103 for cross-border bank wires where the beneficiary holds an account directly with a SWIFT member bank. For local dollar-denominated payroll, the most efficient rail is Panama's Automated Clearing House (ACH), accessed through the local commercial bank, together with direct debit and direct-credit files generated by the payroll SaaS. For larger, documented trade disbursements, a commercial letter of credit (documentary L/C) is available through Panamanian banks, particularly for software licensing, hardware procurement, or regional subcontracting arrangements. Where the client vendor is not SWIFT-connected, disbursement can be routed to a regulated EMI or local partner bank through an aggregated MT103 or other permitted network, but each destination must undergo sanctions and AML screening.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/EUR and USD/GBP forwards for payroll obligations in European currencies
USD/MXN and USD/COP deliverable swap or forward contracts through international bank counterparties
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for Latin American restricted currencies, including Argentine peso, Venezuelan bolívar, and similar controlled currencies
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for long-term intercompany payroll funding arrangements
Plain-vanilla foreign exchange options for hedging projected multi-year payroll disbursement exposure in volatile emerging-market currencies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of Panama through the licensed Resident Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March; no extension or pro-ration for mid-year incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-payment penalty plus monthly interest; no Certificate of Good Standing may be obtained until paid; prolonged non-payment may trigger administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración de Renta – ISR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March following the end of the taxable year; extended due date applies only if DGI approval is obtained
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fines and interest under the Panamanian Tax Code; non-filing blocks issuance of good-standing and tax clearance certificates and may result in escalated administrative penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Confirmation / Final Beneficiary Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI Beneficial Ownership Registry (ReBFO) via the licensed Resident Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March and within 30 days of any shareholding or final-beneficiary change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monetary penalties under Law 23 of 2015 and implementing regulations; inability to obtain good-standing certificates; restrictions on share transfers and registered-agent services for non-compliant entities.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if the S.A. is classified as a DGI Gran Contribuyente, is subject to sectoral regulation (banking, insurance, securities), is listed on the Panama Stock Exchange, or is selected by the DGI under its audit-risk criteria. A non-resident non-operating S.A. with no Panama-source activities is generally exempt.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB and adopted in Panama; IFRS for SMEs permitted for non-publicly accountable S.A.s.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The S.A. must identify and record all final beneficial owners holding 10% or more of shares or control; bearer shares remain immobilized. The resident agent obtains KYC documentation and files the annual sworn UBO confirmation; any share transfer requires an updated register entry and UBO filing within 30 days.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 - USD 8,000 per year if audit requirement is triggered

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No sector-specific tax holiday for ISIC 6201 cybersecurity and payroll software; territorial taxation excludes foreign-derived non-Panama-source revenue; eligible costs of Panamanian-source sales may be deducted, and a deemed expense regime for unreported rental income does not apply to tech companies. No R&D super-deduction available.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 02 (Declaración Jurada de Impuesto sobre la Renta) filed through the DGI T@PA online electronic filing system
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the fiscal year-end; for calendar-year taxpayers the DGI designates staggered due dates in March. Extended returns must be requested through Form 02-EPT before the original deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenues earned from Panamanian-source services and software licensing
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only revenue derived from clients located in Panama or use of software within Panama; exclude foreign-source SaaS revenue under territorial taxation unless a principal purpose or economic nexus rule reclassifies it.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Returns, discounts, and cancellations of payroll services
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct contractual refunds for terminated payroll automation contracts; retain service-level records and contracts for audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Attributable costs of producing Panamanian-source revenue, including cloud hosting, personnel, and payment gateway fees
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only direct and reasonably allocated costs attributable to Panamanian operations; cross-border cost allocations must meet transfer pricing rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable gross profit before permitted deductions and loss carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute profit by subtracting deductible costs from Panamanian-source gross revenue; foreign head-office expenses are deductible only if proportionally attributable to Panamanian-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after applying loss carryforwards, non-taxable foreign-source income excluded, and any special deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the five-year loss carryforward in the submission streamline; attach loss reintegration schedules and proof of foreign-source exclusion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax assessed at 25% of net taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign corporations without a Panamanian permanent establishment are taxable only on Panamanian-source income and must ensure treaty or territorial adjustments are submitted in the schedules to avoid a 25% assessment on gross remittances.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance payments made (estimated corporate income tax instalments) and any credits withheld
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List quarterly advance payments made during the fiscal year; attach bank corroboration and withholding certificates; non-residents are generally not eligible for withholdings on Panamanian services unless a permanent establishment exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net balance payable or refund claimed
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment is due with the Form 02 submission. Non-resident taxpayers may request refunds only after substantiating excess withholding with DGI certification.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 02 attracts a surcharge of 1% per month on the tax due, capped at 30%; DGI additionally imposes fixed late-filing fines under the Fiscal Code ranging from USD 100 to USD 500, and unpaid tax interest accrues at variable Panamanian fiscal interest rates until settlement.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory dividend withholding tax; reduced to 5% for dividends paid from profits that already bore Panamanian corporate income tax at the entity level, and a 0% rate for distributions from companies operating under an approved tax-free zone or securities-exchange listing where applicable.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a Double Taxation Agreement (DTA), the non-resident shareholder must obtain a certificate of tax residence (TRC) from its home jurisdiction and submit it with the Form 03 (Solicitud de Devolución o Compensación) or a withholding-tax reduction request to the DGI before remittance. DGI verifies beneficial ownership, requires a sworn statement of non-Panamanian economic substance, and issues an administrative confirmation enabling the reduced rate. Panama has a narrow treaty network, and treaty relief is not available if the shareholder lacks substantive economic activity in the treaty jurisdiction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid by a Panamanian entity for software licensing or technology used in Panama are Panamanian-source and are subject to a general 25% tax on a deemed 50% taxable base, producing a 12.5% effective withholding rate. Interest paid to non-resident financial institutions not licensed in Panama is generally subject to 10% withholding, while interest on negotiated Panamanian official instruments may be exempt. Treaty reductions apply, but only after validation of the beneficial owner's residence.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 250,000 for aggregate related-party transactions or USD 2,000,000 for annual gross revenue; the taxpayer must prepare contemporaneous Local File and Master File documentation and file the informative transfer pricing return with DGI when either threshold is exceeded.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations (Decree 123 of 2019) apply to entities conducting relevant activities. A payroll SaaS company holding Panamanian IP, financing, or a holding structure must evidence physical office, Panamanian employees, decision-making meetings, and regular management presence. DGI approves a simplified annual substance notification, and failure to show economic substance in Panama for relevant income renders the entity liable to fines, corrective reclassification of foreign income, and denial of treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Under-declaring Panamanian-source revenue from payroll automation clients, disguising it as foreign SaaS revenue, or fabricating deductible costs in offshore service invoices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fiscal Code Articles 731-735 impose fines from 25% to 10 times the evaded tax for serious misdeclaration, plus statutory interest; criminal tax evasion carries imprisonment of 2 to 5 years and a monetary penalty based on the tax amount at risk.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, officers, and beneficial owners who sign false declarations or instruct the under-declaration are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax, surcharges, and criminal fines; the DGI may obtain travel bans and preventive asset freezes before final criminal conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an S.A. with no Panamanian office, no employees, no contracts, and no accounting substance, yet invoicing payroll services to clients in Panama or maintaining Panamanian bank accounts and then asserting corporate insulation from liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Panamanian Economic Substance Rules and the Fiscal Code allow DGI to demand the company's substance, impose fines of up to USD 100,000 for failure to file the economic substance declaration, and disregard juridical personality where the entity is a sham. Courts may levy civil restitution equal to the avoided tax plus 30% of unpaid liabilities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Beneficial owners and statutory directors risk veil-piercing remedies in Panamanian civil courts where inadequate capitalization, commingling of funds, and the absence of corporate formalities have caused damages or tax losses; liability extends to fraudulent transfer of assets and director disqualification in the Public Registry.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / International Wire and Payroll Funds Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Panamanian payroll SaaS platform to move client payroll for shell companies, allowing layering of funds through intermediary Panamanian accounts to conceal beneficial ownership, or failing to maintain auditable transaction trails for ACH and wire payments crossing the Panama banking system.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Legislative Decree 2 of 2019 and Law 21 of 2013 set administrative fines of up to USD 1 million for material AML deficiencies; criminal money laundering, including using digital payment rails and shell invoicing, triggers imprisonment of 5 to 12 years and confiscation of laundered assets under the Panamanian Criminal Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior managers with direct involvement in onboarding payroll clients used for layering are individually liable; the UAF (Financial Analysis Unit) and the Public Ministry may order account seizure, travel restrictions, and a prohibition from serving as directors of regulated Panamanian companies.
